When SpaceX isn't busy recovering rockets, it's apparently placing orders with AI companies. In February this year, the parent company of Starlink brought xAI (which owns the platform formerly known as Twitter, X) under its umbrella. This April, SpaceX signed a partnership with Cursor, a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. And SpaceXAI (its new name) has recently, with Cursor's assistance, launched the Grok Bot and the Grok 4.6 model.

Updated August 14, 2026: SpaceXAI has completed its acquisition of Cursor.

Updated June 16, 2026: One week after going public, SpaceX acquired Cursor.

Below is the updated original report:

SpaceX strikes $10 billion Cursor deal, paving way for subsequent $60 billion acquisition

Cursor has long been a favourite among software engineers who use Macs to write AI programs. It was one of the earliest services to integrate large language model AI into the application development process.

This April, SpaceX and Cursor announced that the two companies were "working closely together, with the goal of creating the world's top AI for coding and knowledge work."

The collaboration originally included a $10 billion payment from SpaceX to Cursor:

Prior to the acquisition this April, Cursor shared more details about the arrangement:

Cursor is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate our model training work. Composer first launched just six months ago as our first agentic coding model. Since then, Composer 1.5 scaled up reinforcement learning by more than 20 times. Composer 2 added continued pre-training to achieve frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost of other models. Every increase in compute has translated into noticeably more powerful models. We've always wanted to push our training work further, but have been constrained by compute. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to dramatically advance the intelligence of our models.

The collaboration between SpaceX and Cursor has strengthened a competitor to agentic coding software such as Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex.
